extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, and investigators of nature (practitioners of inductive method)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for collecting, classifying, and using empirical 'instances' to discover forms and laws of nature (Baconian inductive method), including seven modes of action and twenty-seven prerogative instances for theory and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuance (method of action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of continuance (keeping bodies in particular conditions over time) as a method of action for producing effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect examples of continuance diligently from every quarter. Open vessels are useful for separations, hermetically sealed vessels for mixtures, and partly closed but air-admitting vessels for putrefaction. Observe how confinement impedes motion and how heat (fire) stops mouldiness and other conformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction of motion (method of action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of arresting, repelling, allowing, or directing original motion when one body meets another; includes figure and position of vessels and internal/external operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider vessel shapes (upright vs inverted cone) and curved or alternately contracted/dilated forms. Include strainers and cases where one body within another directs motion (e.g., pebbles collecting muddy particles; egg white gluing grosser particles to refine syrup). Observe applications in casting and modelling. Note examples and counterclaims (e.g., avoid rash attributions like Telesius' on animal formation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony and aversion (sympathy and antipathy) (method of action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Occult and specific correspondences (sympathies/antipathies) between natural objects that cause particular effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate correspondences among substances (e.g., sulphur cluster: sulphur, oil, flame; mercury cluster: mercury, water, air) and between bodies and their supports (climate, soil, depth, menstruum). Examine grafting compatibility, manure propriety, specific foods for animals, and kinds of putrefaction producing animals. Prefer experimentally verified harmonies (magnet/iron, gold/mercury) and medicines with specific effects. Collect tradition and reports honestly but without rash credulity; exterminate fables and superstition. Rare latent harmonies deserve diligent inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternation and interchange of modes (seventh method of action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using alternation/interchange of the other six modes to produce effects; complex chains of actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that series or chain of alternation can be powerful but difficult to trace; reserve detailed examples until deeper investigation of the other methods has been completed. Appreciate that tracing these chains is crucial to larger works and requires patience and deeper inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magical instances (definition and identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where a scanty or small agent produces a disproportionately large or 'miraculous' effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify three ways such effects arise: (1) self-multiplication (e.g., fire, specific poisons, transferred/multiplied motions like wheel-to-wheel), (2) excitation/invitation of another substance (e.g., magnet exciting needles, leaven), (3) excess of rapidity of one motion over another (e.g., gunpowder, cannon, mines). The two former require investigation of harmonies, the latter require measurement of motion. Investigate whether transformations 'per minima' (changing bodies by minimal transfer) are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligent collection of instances from every quarter
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances (observations/experiments) must be gathered widely and diligently to inform induction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not restrict to narrow sources; collect practical and natural observations broadly to illuminate the methods. Prioritize honest reports and tradition cautiously; avoid rash acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exterminate fables / avoid superstition and credulity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject fable-based or superstitious claims when assembling instances or inferring harmonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where alleged sympathies/antipathies have plausible mechanical explanations (e.g., competition for juices among plants), prefer natural explanations. Require experimental verification for claims of sympathy/antipathy; discard those mixed with fable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate correspondences between bodies and their supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine how bodies correspond with the climate, soil, depth, and other supporting media in which they are produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inquire into where each metal, gem, plant, or tree is generated and thrives; test various manures and soils; examine grafting readiness across species; these correspondences can elucidate affinities and causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe coition/union and readiness to mix
rubrics_metrics.description: Record how readily bodies cohere or resist mixture and how parts distribute/digest when mingled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note examples (powders mix with water, chalk/ashes with oils) and study collocation, distribution, digestion of parts after mixing, and predominance after mixture. These observations illuminate composition behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of synoptical tables in forming tables of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize collected instances into synoptical tables for specific natures to facilitate induction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search out prerogative instances with zeal and place them in the synoptic table; collect some instances only after these tables are formed. Tables serve as the work of the interpreter and help select the most valuable instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value quality over quantity in instances
rubrics_metrics.description: A few prerogative (privileged) instances are far more valuable than a multitude of ordinary instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out those instances 'honored and gifted with prerogatives'—they act like the soul amid the crowd; a few such instances can outweigh many ordinary facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of collection for certain prerogative instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Some prerogative instances should be collected immediately without waiting for special investigation; others can wait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect immediately: similar, singular, deviating, bordering instances; instances of power; instances of the gate; suggesting instances; generally useful instances; and magical instances. The remainder should be gathered after forming synoptical tables for the particular nature under study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances assist senses or the understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Prerogative instances are specially useful because they either assist the senses or the understanding in induction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instances of the lamp for senses; use solitary instances to expedite arriving at forms; use migrating, conspicuous, accompanying, and subjunctive instances to confine or indicate the affirmative; use clandestine and singular instances to elevate the understanding toward general natures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solitary instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Solitary instances expedite the exclusive mode of arriving at the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They help the understanding by more directly pointing to the form; use them early to narrow possibilities when seeking a form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Migrating instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Migrating instances confine and more immediately indicate the affirmative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples across minerals/plants/animals where a nature 'migrates' between gradations to help locate shared properties and laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuous (ostensive) instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Conspicuous instances indicate the affirmative clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ ostensive cases that plainly exhibit the property under inquiry to limit hypothesis space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clandestine instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Clandestine instances elevate the understanding and lead toward general and common natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cases where the property is hidden or less apparent but, when exposed, reveal deeper principles; they help generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutive instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitutive instances nearly elevate the understanding toward general natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ instances that show constitutive features of a nature (close to direct exemplification of the form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Similar instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of similarity that group individualities by common properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect similar instances immediately; they help to classify and identify common properties, though they may elevate the understanding less directly than clandestine or singular instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Single notable instances that can lift the understanding toward general truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather striking or unique examples that can suggest forms or laws; include them early in collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviating instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that deviate from the general pattern and thus correct the understanding's habits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use deviations to test and correct hasty generalizations; collect early to avoid being misled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bordering instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that border between kinds and lead to grand forms or fabric of the universe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study cases at boundaries of classification to discover overarching forms; collect these early as they are especially informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of power
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that show where to commence in practice and help avoid repeating others' labors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to identify starting points for experiments or interventions; they are practical guides for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompanying and hostile instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that accompany a property or are hostile/opposed to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accompanying instances to confirm relations and hostile instances to guard against false attributions; they help in delimiting causal connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjunctive instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that, by their particular conditional relation, indicate the affirmative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ subjunctive or conditional cases to test necessary or contingent relations in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of alliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that elevate the understanding by showing close alliances between natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use allied cases that reveal unifying principles across different subjects; these raise understanding toward general natures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of the cross and instances of divorce
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that guard the understanding from false forms and causes by showing crossing or separation of properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross and divorce instances to refute or eliminate spurious causes and to discriminate between coincident and causal relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of the gate
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that serve as portals to understanding or to practical beginnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect these early (they are among those to be gathered immediately); they indicate where to enter an inquiry or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that cite or point to relevant phenomena or precedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cited cases to support inferences and to link new observations to established facts or laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of the road (instances of the course)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances indicating the course or progression of phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ these to trace sequences, gradations, or developmental paths that illuminate latent processes and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary instances (doses of nature, lancing instances, instances of the rod)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that measure, point, or supplement the inquiry (including mathematical instances that 'measure' the matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mathematical and other measurement-like instances to quantify and bound the problem; the four mathematical instances measure practice. Supplementary instances help refine or test hypotheses practically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrestling instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that test or 'wrestle' with a nature to reveal its limits or force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forceful or stress-testing cases to reveal hidden properties and to distinguish essential from accidental features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that induce aspiration and suggest possible achievable aims for practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect these early; they encourage aiming for possible results and inform experimental goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generally useful instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of broad practical value that assist practice or elevate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather these early; they directly inform useful applications and practical improvements.
